objective: Define a measurable baseline for meeting or exceeding relevant industry, federal, defense, software-supply-chain, application-security, AI-governance, and operational-evidence standards without overstating maturity.
claims_boundary: This baseline records target standards, control intent, evidence gates, and current gaps. It does not establish certification, accreditation, CMMC conformity, NIST SP 800-171 implementation, DFARS satisfaction, FedRAMP authorization, ISO certification, SOC 2 attestation, BAE validation, DOE validation, supplier approval, export-control clearance, classified access, external reproduction, hardware performance, field performance, or operational authority.

stance.meet_or_exceed_rule: A requirement is not marked MET or EXCEEDED until mapped evidence exists, automated checks pass where applicable, and any required independent or formal assessment evidence is attached.
stance.prediction_rule: Forecasted industry demand may guide preparation, but it never upgrades capability maturity or compliance status.
stance.partner_rule: Partner or prime relevance may be recorded as a screening hypothesis only; it is not validation, acceptance, or endorsement.
stance.cui_rule: No CUI/CDI handling is claimed until the system boundary, asset inventory, control implementation, SSP, assessment evidence, and authorization route are documented.

standard_sources.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
standard_sources.baseline_target: Map SARA governance, identify/protect/detect/respond/recover controls, and maintain evidence for each material system risk.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Tie each control to CI evidence, audit events, recovery evidence, and owner-reviewed risk disposition.

standard_sources.name: NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework
standard_sources.baseline_target: Map software development practices to prepare the organization, protect software, produce well-secured software, and respond to vulnerabilities.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Require CI artifacts, dependency evidence, release index custody, vulnerability response workflow, and claims-boundary enforcement for each release.

standard_sources.name: NIST SP 800-171 Revision 3
standard_sources.baseline_target: Use Revision 3 requirements as forward-looking CUI readiness controls while preserving non-claim status.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Maintain SSP-ready evidence, asset boundaries, control implementation status, assessment artifacts, POA&M, and external assessment route before CUI handling claims.

standard_sources.name: NIST SP 800-171A Revision 3 assessment procedures
standard_sources.baseline_target: Map each security requirement to objective assessment methods and evidence objects.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Prebuild assessment evidence packages with traceable artifact IDs, reviewer decisions, and deficiency handling.

standard_sources.name: NIST SP 800-172 Revision 3 enhanced CUI requirements
standard_sources.baseline_target: Track enhanced CUI requirements for high-value defense-system screening without claiming implementation.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Design optional enhanced safeguards for advanced persistent threat resistance, segmented environments, stronger monitoring, and mission-assurance overlays.

standard_sources.name: DoD CMMC Program / 32 CFR Part 170
standard_sources.baseline_target: Track CMMC Level 1/2/3 applicability and route to appropriate self-assessment, third-party assessment, or government assessment when contractually required.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Keep CMMC status separate from internal CI evidence and require formal assessment status before any CMMC claim.

standard_sources.name: NIST SP 800-161 Revision 1 Update 1
standard_sources.baseline_target: Map suppliers, dependencies, build systems, external services, provenance, and supplier risk handling.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Tie supplier/dependency risk to SBOM, dependency freeze evidence, release artifacts, vulnerability status, and owner risk decisions.

standard_sources.name: Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts specification
standard_sources.baseline_target: Map build provenance and artifact generation to SLSA source/build tracks.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Require hosted, tamper-resistant provenance, source-to-build traceability, artifact digest custody, and independent verification route before higher-level claims.

standard_sources.name: OpenSSF Scorecard
standard_sources.baseline_target: Use Scorecard-style controls as open-source repository hygiene inputs.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Add automated branch protection, pinned dependencies/actions, token permission minimization, vulnerability scanning, maintained metadata, and signed-release evidence where possible.

standard_sources.name: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 5.0
standard_sources.baseline_target: Map web/API surfaces to ASVS verification controls for authentication, authorization, session, input, API, cryptography, errors, and configuration.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Require testable API controls, negative tests, threat modeling, authz boundary checks, audit-log checks, and no-secret exposure for exposed surfaces.

standard_sources.name: OWASP CycloneDX BOM standard
standard_sources.domain: software bill of materials and supply-chain transparency
standard_sources.baseline_target: Generate or ingest SBOM evidence for releases and attach artifact digests.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Include SBOM, VEX/affectedness posture, build provenance, component risk decisions, and release-index linkage.

standard_sources.name: SPDX 3 specification
standard_sources.domain: software package data exchange / SBOM interoperability
standard_sources.baseline_target: Support SPDX-compatible SBOM interchange where partner or customer workflows require it.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Maintain CycloneDX and SPDX compatibility strategy with clear artifact formats and validation records.

standard_sources.name: OpenVEX / VEX vulnerability affectedness statements
standard_sources.baseline_target: Track vulnerability affectedness separately from raw vulnerability presence.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Publish or retain VEX-ready internal records only when affected/not-affected analysis is evidenced and reviewer-approved.

standard_sources.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
standard_sources.baseline_target: Map AI-assisted workflow risks to governance, mapping, measurement, and management functions.
standard_sources.exceed_target: Require model-use boundaries, human authorization, evidence provenance, evaluation records, red-team/adversarial cases where applicable, and no autonomous high-impact actions without approval.

minimum_redlines: No certification or conformity claim without formal evidence.
No CUI/CDI handling claim without a documented system boundary and control evidence.
No BAE, DOE, partner, supplier, or government validation claim from thematic overlap or internal CI evidence.
No autonomous external action without human authorization and audit record.
No public release package without claims-boundary text.
No release index without artifact digest custody.
No dependency or supplier acceptance without provenance and risk review.
No AI capability claim without evaluation scope, limitations, and human review boundary.
No hardware, field, laboratory, or operational-performance claim without reproducible measurement evidence.

readiness_levels.meaning: Control objective, owner, and applicability are defined.
Internal implementation evidence or CI artifact exists.
Automated gate validates the evidence on every relevant run.
Evidence package is ready for external reviewer or assessor.
A recognized third-party, government, or formal assessment record supports the claim.

target_global_readiness: L4_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW_READY before partner/prime submission; L5_FORMALLY_ASSESSED only where applicable and evidenced
